paper_metadata.title: Refractory epilepsy in a Chinese population

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses a consecutive, unselected sample from a regional hospital neurology clinic, which is well-described. However, as the authors acknowledge, hospital-based samples are subject to referral bias, potentially over-representing refractory cases compared to the general population. Baseline characteristics are provided, but the participation rate of eligible individuals is not explicitly stated.

items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: unselected patients over the age of 14 years with epilepsy from a Neurology clinic at a regional hospital, the Prince of Wales hospital in Hong Kong, China that caters for a population of 800,000.
items.reasoning: The source population and its geographic/demographic context (Hong Kong, 97% ethnic Chinese) are clearly defined.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: Prognostic factors (MTS, mental retardation, etc.) were measured using standardized ILAE criteria and high-resolution MRI. The use of a single neurologist for data entry and a radiologist for MRI review ensures consistency.

items.reasoning: The study uses internationally recognized ILAE definitions for the prognostic factors.

items.reasoning: The use of high-resolution MRI and dual-specialist review (neurologist and radiologist) provides high reliability.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (refractory epilepsy) is clearly defined based on established clinical criteria (failure of 2 AEDs). Measurement was performed prospectively during routine clinic visits, which is standard for this type of study.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Refractory epilepsy was defined as the presence of one or more seizures despite the use of two appropriate AEDs.
items.reasoning: The definition is explicit and follows common clinical standards.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: at each visit, seizure frequency, response to drug therapy and compliance were routinely recorded.
items.reasoning: Prospective recording of seizure frequency during clinical follow-up is the standard method for determining refractory status.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: In our clinic at each visit, seizure frequency, response to drug therapy and compliance were routinely recorded.
items.reasoning: All patients were followed in the same neurology clinic using the same recording protocol.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses multivariable logistic regression to adjust for several key factors (age, sex, aetiology, mental retardation). However, the authors admit they could not accurately measure the number of seizures prior to treatment, which is a known major confounder in epilepsy prognosis.

items.label: Important Confounders Measured
items.prompt: All important confounders, including treatments (key variables in conceptual model: LIST), are measured.
items.evidence_snippet: we were unable in all cases to determine accurately the number of seizures before treatment was started and therefore did not incorporate this variable into the analysis.
items.reasoning: While age, sex, and aetiology were measured, a critical prognostic factor (pre-treatment seizure frequency) was omitted.
